answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut, incumbent refuses to reopen pricing, contract expires in 14 days, and we have capacity for exactly one action this cycle. Memory_c2 documents that switching primary supply to a low-cost vendor previously drove a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Verifying c2 confirms that prior migration did not introduce material service or billing risk, which directly supports using the one available decision slot to move primary supply to a low-cost vendor. Re-verifying the incumbent-renewal and multi-year memories is lower-value here because the incumbent has already refused to renegotiate. Adding a second source (c3) or renewing (c1) does not satisfy the mandated cost cut and would consume the single decision slot on lower-leverage moves. Deferring (c5) is not viable with a 14-day expiry and no auto-renewal. The new context—incumbent refusal to reprice—supersedes the prior pattern captured in c4; renegotiation is not available this cycle. Given the 94% line utilization with no buffer, the switch should be scoped as a guarded migration with parallel-run or qualification steps and a documented rollback path, to control delivery risk while securing the required cost reduction.
